title: Consolidate Strava Handlers Into One Catch-All
userRequest: api/ contained exactly 12 serverless handler files, which is Vercel's Hobby-tier ceiling for a single deployment. The next feature needing an endpoint could not deploy at all — social-foundation was hard-blocked behind it. Strava was the natural place to reclaim slots: four small handlers sharing one _lib/strava.ts and one client.
description:
Collapsed api/strava/{activities,callback,disconnect,exchange}.ts into a single Vercel catch-all at api/strava/[...route].ts that resolves the first path segment and dispatches, 404-ing an unknown segment. Handler count went 12 to 9, which is the headroom social-foundation needs (it lands at 10).

The public paths are unchanged, which was the whole constraint. The iOS client calls these four URLs and /api/strava/callback is registered with Strava as the Authorization Callback Domain, so a dropped route breaks OAuth for every new connection. Each body moved across verbatim: identical status codes and JSON error keys (the client branches on missing_device_key, missing_code_or_device_key, method_not_allowed), the same console.error tags so log greps keep working, the deliberate 200 connected:false non-error response in activities, and the CODE_RE / ERROR_RE validation plus fixed-scheme redirect in callback, which is security-relevant input validation guarding against query-param injection into otterpace://strava-callback.

The refactor moves routing from the filesystem, where it could not be wrong, into a switch, where it can. So the existing 20 handler tests were rewired to dispatch THROUGH the catch-all rather than importing handlers directly — they now exercise routing as well as bodies, and any segment that stops dispatching fails its whole suite. A new routing guard asserts every previously-public path dispatches (never 404), an unknown segment 404s rather than falling into a real route, a nested path still resolves on its first segment, and the OAuth callback still 302s into the app scheme.

Verified the iOS client's four URLs match the served segments exactly and that no docs referenced the deleted files.

Glossary: the four entries pointing at the deleted handler files were removed (they were in fact blocking the workflow with a glossary save error) and replaced with entries for the catch-all and its four route functions.

Note for future backend work: this stack's codeyam test registry tracks the swift runner only (stack.json test = swift test), so the 205 vitest backend tests carry no registry evidence. That is pre-existing, but it means the audit's missingTests result speaks only to Swift coverage.
